short: Proclaimed queen to keep England Protestant, and deposed within nine days.
full:
Edward VI, dying of tuberculosis at fifteen, drew up a device for the succession that excluded his Catholic half-sister Mary and settled the crown on Jane Grey, his cousin and a committed Protestant, who had been married to the Duke of Northumberland's son weeks earlier. Edward died on 6 July 1553 and Jane was proclaimed queen on 10 July.

The plan failed almost at once. Mary, who had avoided arrest, raised support in East Anglia; the council in London changed sides, and Northumberland's small army melted away. On 19 July Mary was proclaimed instead, and Jane became a prisoner in the Tower, where she had been lodged as queen. She might have survived it. Wyatt's rebellion in January 1554, raised against Mary's Spanish marriage by a group that included Jane's own father, made her too dangerous to keep alive. She was beheaded on 12 February 1554, aged about seventeen.
